sum: - Zacks Research upgraded Vodafone Group from “strong sell” to “hold.”
- Analyst views remain mixed: four rate the stock Buy, four Hold and four Sell; the consensus is Hold with an average price target of $13.13.
- Vodafone shares rose 4.2% and opened at $16.28 on Tuesday.

Vodafone Group (NASDAQ:VOD - Get Free Report) was upgraded by equities researchers at Zacks Research from a "strong sell" rating to a "hold" rating in a research note issued to investors on Tuesday, Zacks reports.

Other research analysts have also issued research reports about the company. Barclays lowered Vodafone Group from an "equal weight" rating to an "underweight" rating in a report on Tuesday, October 20th. The Goldman Sachs Group upgraded Vodafone Group from a "sell" rating to a "buy" rating in a report on Friday, September 4th. Weiss Ratings lowered Vodafone Group from a "hold (c)" rating to a "hold (c-)" rating in a research report on Friday, October 30th. Wall Street Zen cut Vodafone Group from a "buy" rating to a "hold" rating in a research note on Tuesday, September 22nd. Finally, JPMorgan Chase & Co. reaffirmed a "sell" rating on shares of Vodafone Group in a report on Monday, July 27th. Four research analysts have rated the stock with a Buy rating, four have issued a Hold rating and four have issued a Sell rating to the stock. According to MarketBeat, Vodafone Group currently has a consensus rating of "Hold" and an average price target of $13.13.

VOD stock opened at $16.28 on Tuesday. The company has a current ratio of 1.14, a quick ratio of 1.11 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.84. The business has a 50-day simple moving average of $16.35 and a two-hundred day simple moving average of $15.40. Vodafone Group has a 52-week low of $11.21 and a 52-week high of $17.71.

Several large investors have recently made changes to their positions in VOD. Sei Investments Co. raised its stake in shares of Vodafone Group by 72.4% in the first quarter. Sei Investments Co. now owns 866,316 shares of the cell phone carrier's stock valued at $13,014,000 after buying an additional 363,694 shares during the period. Merit Financial Group LLC lifted its position in shares of Vodafone Group by 7,003.0% during the 2nd quarter.

sum: Trending Stocks Today, November 3, 2026: PC Jeweller, Trident, Vodafone Idea, YES Bank

Mumbai, November 3: Shares of Trident, PC Jeweller, Vodafone Idea and YES Bank featured among the most actively traded stocks by volume on the NSE on Tuesday, November 3. Trident surged nearly 9% after reporting a sharp rise in September-quarter profit and announcing a proposed Rs 4,650-crore capacity expansion programme. Vodafone Idea edged higher, extending the previous session’s gains, despite a TRAI financial disincentive, while PC Jeweller and YES Bank traded lower amid regulatory and legal developments.

PC Jeweller shares remained under pressure on Tuesday, extending their decline from Monday after the company disclosed over the weekend that the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) had issued administrative warning letters to its managing director and company secretary for failing to maintain a structured digital database as required under regulatory norms.
The lapse pertained to the company’s business update for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, which contained unpublished price-sensitive information (UPSI).

In an exchange filing dated October 31, PC Jeweller said the warning letters were issued on October 30 to promoter and managing director Balram Garg and company secretary and compliance officer Vijay Panwar.

The company clarified that while the structured digital database had not been maintained in connection with the business update, its trading window remained closed for designated persons and their immediate relatives throughout the relevant period. It added that the regulatory action would have no financial or operational bearing on its business.

The share price weakness comes despite an improvement in the company’s recent financial performance and its announcement earlier in October that it had settled its outstanding debt with a consortium of 14 banks.

Here’s my top FTSE 100 telecoms stock (and it’s not Vodafone or BT)
sum: Airtel Africa (LSE:AAF) might not be the most famous name on the FTSE 100, but its share price performance over the past five years has been nothing short of remarkable.

Since October 2021, the telecoms group has seen its market-cap nearly treble. It's the sort of result that would make shareholders in BT and Vodafone, another two Footsie stocks in the sector, extremely jealous. But I don't think the party's over yet…

In October, the company separately listed its money division, formally known as Airtel Mobile Commerce. It provides a financial services platform that enables users to send, receive, and store money directly on their mobile phones without needing a traditional bank account. In rural Africa, it's been a real game changer.

Airtel Africa retains a 77.85% interest in the business, which currently (2 November) has a market-cap of £5.08bn. Airtel Africa itself is valued at £9.94bn. This is very close to the group's pre-separation valuation. In other words, spinning out its money business has had no impact. Not yet, anyway.

However, looking ahead, I think it could be a smart move. Historically, telecoms companies have attracted lower valuations than other sectors. But Airtel Money is more akin to a rapidly-growing technology company. Indeed, its first set of results as a standalone entity were impressive.
During the six months to 30 September, customer numbers increased 18.7% to 56.7m. And compared to the same period a year earlier, revenue was 34% higher. Basic earnings per share (EPS) jumped 21.1%.
Additionally, the company declared its first dividend and is aiming to return a massive 80% of earnings to shareholders each year. Of course, payouts are never guaranteed.

Vodafone Shares Fall 3.7% Following SpaceX Spectrum Deal and VodafoneThree Investor Briefing
sum: Vodafone Group (LSE:VOD) shares declined 3.7% to 119.75 pence on Friday, as investors assessed developments in the telecommunications sector and updated financial targets announced at the company's VodafoneThree Investor Briefing.

The decline followed news that SpaceX had agreed to acquire a portfolio of low-band wireless spectrum in the United States, a development that has drawn attention to potential changes in competition between satellite communications providers and established mobile network operators.

The transaction has raised questions about the longer-term competitive implications of satellite-based connectivity services for traditional telecommunications businesses, although the direct financial impact on Vodafone remains uncertain.
Vodafone shares also came under pressure following Thursday's investor briefing, during which the company outlined revised financial and operational objectives for its merged UK mobile business.

The company increased its annual cost savings target for VodafoneThree to £1 billion by the financial year ending 2032, compared with its previous objective of £700 million by the financial year ending 2030.
Vodafone also introduced a target for adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation after leases (EBITDAaL) to grow at a mid-to-high single-digit annual rate through FY2032.
The revised objectives reflect the company's plans to deliver additional efficiencies and improve profitability following the combination of Vodafone's UK operations with Three.

The brokerage expects Vodafone Idea’s EBITDA to expand at a 15% compound annual growth rate, marginally better than its earlier trajectory. However, it cautioned that the projected growth will come off a relatively low base as the company’s operating metrics gradually recover.
Its assessment suggests that Vodafone Idea is currently placing greater emphasis on rebuilding its customer base and improving retention rather than maximising near-term revenue.

Vodafone takes full ownership of VodafoneThree
sum: Vodafone Group Plc (“Vodafone”) announces that it has completed the buyout of CK Hutchison Group Telecom Holding Limited’s (“CKHGT”) 49% stake in VodafoneThree (the “Transaction”), for £4.3 billion (€4.9 billion). As a result, Vodafone now owns 100% of VodafoneThree, the UK’s largest mobile operator and one of the fastest growing broadband providers.
The Transaction has been fully funded from existing Vodafone Group cash resources.

Full ownership of VodafoneThree will enable us to move at an even faster pace and capture the significant benefits created through our £11 billion network investment plan and targeted synergies, including £700 million of annual cost and capital expenditure synergies by FY30.

Margherita Della Valle, Chief Executive of Vodafone Group, said: “With full ownership and control, we’ll have the ability to move faster in the next phase of building one of Europe’s leading networks. This best-in-class infrastructure will deliver better connectivity for our customers up and down the country, help drive the UK's digital economy, and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.”

On 8 October 2026, Vodafone will be hosting a VodafoneThree Investor Briefing. The briefing will outline VodafoneThree’s strategy, growth ambitions and the significant value creation we expect to deliver over the coming years, as we focus on building the UK’s best network.
The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of Vodafone is Maaike de Bie, Group General Counsel and Company Secretary (Tel: +44 (0)1635 33251).
- Vodafone funded the £4.3 billion (€4.9 billion) of cash consideration from existing cash resources.

Vodafone (Q2 Results): guidance raised
sum: First-quarter revenue rose 9.7% to €10.3bn, with growth boosted by the addition of Three UK revenue. Organic Service revenue growth was 5.2% to €8.6bn, with all segments contributing positively.
Adjusted cash profit (EBITDAaL) rose 6.2% organically to €2.9bn, with margins up 0.6 percentage points to 28.5%.

Full-year guidance has been updated to include nine months of Safaricom following completion of the transaction. Vodafone now expects adjusted cash profit of €13.0-13.3bn and free cash flow of €2.6-2.9bn, with performance expected at the upper end of both ranges.

Vodafone’s first quarter was another step in the right direction. Growth was broad-based, and there’s new guidance that suggests upgrades to consensus. The turnaround is gaining credibility, but there’s still work to be done.

Sales in the telecom sector should be relatively robust, as broadband and mobile services are hardly optional. Yet, over the last decade, telecom giants have had to pump huge sums of cash into building out fibre networks and snapping up parts of the 5G spectrum. The main challenge has been the low sales growth relative to spending in telecoms compared to other sectors.

In response to several years of underperformance, Vodafone has evolved its strategy. There have been job cuts, the merger of its UK business with Three UK, and sales of the underperforming Spanish and Italian divisions.

Vodafone also plans to buy the remaining 49% stake in VodafoneThree. The original agreement included an option to acquire the stake after three years, so moving after just one year suggests confidence in the early integration progress. Owning the whole business should make it easier to move quickly and capture the planned benefits, but it also increases Vodafone’s financial exposure if delivery falls short.

Vodafone shares surge 13% after Xavier Niel's £4.4 billion investment. What's next for the stock?
sum: Vodafone (VOD.UK) shares jumped more than 11% on Friday after one of the largest transactions in the European telecommunications sector in recent years was announced. Vega, an investment vehicle controlled by the family of French telecom billionaire Xavier Niel, agreed to acquire Emirates Telecommunications Group's (e&) entire 16.2% stake in Vodafone for approximately £4.4 billion (€5.1 billion / around $6 billion).

At first glance, the market's reaction appeared to be driven simply by the acquisition price. However, investors saw much more than just a premium over Vodafone's previous share price. For many market participants, the transaction represents a strong vote of confidence from one of Europe's most experienced telecom investors, suggesting that Vodafone still has considerable untapped value.
Following regulatory approvals, Vega will become Vodafone's largest shareholder, replacing e&, which is exiting its investment entirely.

Importantly, Xavier Niel emphasized that he has no intention of acquiring the entire company. Under the UK Takeover Code, Vega has confirmed that the investment is intended to be a long-term strategic minority holding designed to support Vodafone's future development rather than gain control of the business.

That distinction matters. Markets typically view short-term financial investors very differently from strategic industry specialists with decades of operational experience. In this case, Vodafone is gaining a shareholder that has successfully built and developed some of Europe's largest telecommunications businesses.
The purchase price suggests Vodafone may have been undervalued
The shares were purchased at approximately 110.5 pence per share, in addition to Vodafone's final dividend.

sum: Vodafone Group stock (ISIN GB00BH4HKS39) is trading close to multi-year highs, with the share price around 125.60 pence on the London Stock Exchange as of September 7, 2026, up about 2.7 percent on the day according to market data.Investing.com UK This strength reflects investors' response to a multi-year turnaround strategy and to new plans for a UK TV offering that aim to boost cross-selling and customer retention.Invezz

The most recent reported figures show that Vodafone generated revenue of 8.62 billion euros in the first fiscal quarter, up from 7.8 billion euros in the same period a year earlier, an increase of roughly 10.5 percent according to analysis from Invezz. The improvement is attributed in part to strong performance in the company’s African and Turkish operations, which have become more important growth drivers in the group’s portfolio.Invezz

Germany remains Vodafone’s largest single market, contributing about 2.7 billion euros of revenue in that first fiscal quarter, which represents growth of 1.9 percent compared with the prior-year period.Invezz In the UK, revenue reached approximately 1.98 billion euros in the same quarter, underlining that the home market is also growing on a reported basis.Invezz For investors, these figures matter because they show that the turnaround is not confined to one geography but is visible in both core European markets and faster-growing regions.

As part of the turnaround, Vodafone has exited some lower-margin markets while strengthening positions in core territories. The company sold its operations in Italy and Spain, raising over 12 billion euros from these disposals according to Invezz. The strategic aim is to reduce exposure to highly competitive markets with weaker returns and to concentrate capital on countries such as Germany and the UK where it sees better long-term prospects.Invezz
